prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map reveals a compact corner alcove with a multi-tiered wall shelf ahead and to the right (roughly 0.8 to 1.5 metres away), bounded by a very close right-hand side wall (0.3 to 0.6 metres) and a stone floor below (1.2 to 1.8 metres). In frames 1 and 2, a shirtless man stands immediately in front and to the left of the camera wearer at roughly 0.4 to 0.8 metres—within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the middle shelf tier—facing away toward the shelf and partially occluding the lower left person in frame 1 and the left side of the alcove. Across frames 3 to 5, the man steps back to roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres on the left while turning his body and head to face and look upward toward the camera wearer, as the camera wearer's own right hand and held yellow fruit appear in the lower foreground of frames 4 and 5 at 0.2 to 0.4 metres, within arm's reach of the man's outstretched right hand (about 0.1 to 0.3 metres apart in frame 5). Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map more clearly separates the foreground person and extending hands from the cluttered background shelf and quantifies the receding floor plane in frame 3's downward tilt. However, the map is unreliable where relative depth rescales across frames—making the upper framed picture and right wall appear artificially bright and closer than the floor in frames 3 and 4—and where it smooths over fine object boundaries like the brass lamps and plates on the tiers.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map outlines the spatial footprint of the foreground man on the left and several small objects on the tiered shelves to the right, set against the unlabelled alcove walls and floor. In frames 1 and 2, the man's mask occupies the left half of the view at roughly 0.4 to 0.8 metres from the camera wearer as he faces right toward the shelf and reaches his right arm across to the middle tier (about 0.5 metres from his torso), while small masks on the top shelf (0.8 to 1.2 metres away, above the framed picture) and a circular plate on the lower shelf (about 1.0 to 1.2 metres away, below his outstretched arm) sit within his arm's reach. In frames 4 and 5, after the man retreats to about 1.0 to 1.5 metres on the left and turns to face and look at the camera wearer, his mask shows his lower legs partly cut off by the bottom frame edge and his right hand extending down toward the lower-centre foreground within arm's reach of the camera wearer. While the segmentation masks sharply isolate the man's silhouette and the round red flower plate from the busy background textures in frames 2 and 4, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence. Specifically, it completely fails to detect any people or objects in frame 3, misses the camera wearer's hands and fruit in frames 4 and 5, misclassifies the entire background room as a dining table in frame 4, and mislabels the flower plate as a pizza, the hanging bag as a bottle, and the brass lamp as a wine glass.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map tracks the 2D joint positions and body orientation of the man standing to the left of the tiered alcove shelf across the sequence. In frame 2, a partial yellow upper-body skeleton places the man at roughly 0.6 to 0.8 metres in front and to the left of the camera wearer, facing right in profile (away from the camera wearer) with his right shoulder, elbow, and wrist extended horizontally to the right into the middle shelf tier within his arm's reach, while his lower body is occluded or out of view. In frame 5, a full-body skeleton shows that the man has stepped back to roughly 1.2 to 1.5 metres on the left and rotated to face the camera wearer directly, with his facial keypoints oriented upward toward the camera wearer, his left arm hanging down by his hip, and his right arm reaching forward and down toward the lower-centre frame within arm's reach of the camera wearer's hand (roughly 0.2 metres apart). This skeletal representation makes the man's torso rotation, head orientation, and exact limb articulation in frames 2 and 5 much easier to read at a glance than in the darkly lit RGB frames. However, the pose map is unreliable in frames 1, 3, and 4 where all body and hand skeletons are completely missing despite the man and the camera wearer's hands being visible in the RGB strip, and it fails to render magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's close-up hands in frames 4 and 5.
